terms.grammar: conjunction, with the perfect indicative; the future perfect for the future
evidence: Cato Agr. 48.2: simul herbae incēperint nāscī, eximitō

terms.gloss: as soon as, the first moment
evidence: Sen. Ep. 104.6: ut prīmum gravitātem urbis excessī
Caes. B.G. 4.12: hostēs, ubi prīmum nostrōs equitēs cōnspexērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Quam prīmum is different: “as soon as possible”.

phrases.latin: crēbrō runcātō. simul herbae incēperint nāscī, eximitō
phrases.english: weed often; as soon as weeds begin to grow, pull them out

phrases.latin: hāc rē vidēre nostra mala nōn possumus; aliī simul dēlinquunt, cēnsōrēs sumus
phrases.english: that is why we cannot see our own faults; as soon as others go wrong, we are their judges

phrases.latin: ut prīmum gravitātem urbis excessī et illum odōrem culīnārum fūmantium … prōtinus mūtātam valētūdinem sēnsī
phrases.english: as soon as I had left the heavy air of the city and that smell of smoking kitchens, I felt my health change at once

sources: Lewis & Short: simul · Lewis & Short: primus · Lewis & Short: ubi · Lewis & Short: ut · Lewis & Short: cum
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cato, loci-phaedrus, loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-terentius), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
